text:
Maria - Sales: Quick heads-up: Concord (prospect) asked for a POC perf run this week — they want sustained inference numbers for their chat frontend: target 300 qps steady, 1k burst, 99th latency < 600ms. Can we confirm an ops plan?
Jamie (SE): I can own the test harness. Plan: k6 for steady HTTP + a separate spike script. 30m steady then a 10m spike. Need an endpoint with a pinned model and KV cache enabled.
Alex S: For repeatability and clean metrics let's run on a Dedicated pool pinned to model-v2.1-quant. Minimizes noisy neighbor variance. Concord said hosted is preferable but they'll accept Dedicated for SLA.
Maria - Sales: Procurement also wants a rough monthly cost if they sustain 300 qps 24/7 vs reserved capacity. Any back-of-envelope?
Oliver (SRE): Rough calc: 300 qps -> ~3M tokens/day (assuming ~120 tokens/request) -> hosted metered spend ~= $X,XXX/day. Reserved commit typically ~25-35% discount. I'll pull finance numbers and confirm.
Priya - Security: Concord's security team asked about KMS, audit logs, and VPC options. For a Dedicated POC we can offer customer-managed KMS + VPC peering. I'll draft a 2-paragraph FAQ for their security questionnaire.
Jamie (SE): Test commands:
```
# steady run (pacing to hit 300 qps total)
k6 run --vus 150 --duration 30m steady.js
# spike run
k6 run --vus 1000 --duration 10m spike.js
```
steady.js will enforce request pacing and record p50/p95/p99, tokens/request.
Maria - Sales: SRE can you provision the ded endpoint and pin to v2.1-quant with prefix KV cache? Also enable tracing header so we can correlate latencies.
Oliver (SRE): Provisioning now. Config: autoscale off, replicas=6, cache TTL=300s, tracing via x-trace-id. Will hand off endpoint URL by EOD.
Maria - Sales: Concord asked for an example runbook for their infra team. Jamie, can you prepare a 1-page runbook + a short summary one-pager with results and cost estimate?
Jamie (SE): Yup. I'll include validation: p99 < 600ms and fallback plan: if p99 > 800ms then reduce max sequence length and enable model_variant=v2.1-quant-fast. Also include CSV artifacts.
Alex S: Also ensure token-level metering is enabled so we can export tokens/sec for pricing calc.
deploy-bot: Deployment created: dedicated/pools/concord-poc by oliver — endpoint at https://ded.redwood.example/concord-poc (status: healthy).
Oliver (SRE): Endpoint ready. Doing warmup now. Expect warm state by 14:10 PT.
Maria - Sales: Goal: deliver initial results within 24h. We'll run 2 tests (AM steady, PM stress) and send one-pager with p50/p95/p99, throughput, tokens/request, and cost estimate.
Jamie (SE): First steady 30m run results: p50=62ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms, throughput=305 qps steady, avg tokens/request=120. Saving CSV to artifacts. Running spike in ~15m.
Priya - Security: Drafted FAQ on KMS and logs. Attaching SOC2 summary. If they ask for HSM, let me know so I can escalate.
Oliver (SRE): Spike run completed. Sustained 1k qps for ~7 minutes before tail microbursts. Observed p99 peak ~1.1s during microbursts, but under sustained 1k qps the p99 settled to ~520ms. We limited new node churn by capping cold-start concurrency.
Maria - Sales: Summary for Concord: steady-state meets their 99th target; spike produces transient tail >600ms but steady periods are within SLA. Suggested mitigations: reserved capacity, prefix caching, sequence-length cap, and fallback to fast variant in routing policy.
Jamie (SE): I'll assemble the one-pager and attach steady.csv and spike.csv. Will include runbook.md with test commands and a short troubleshooting checklist.
Maria - Sales: Please cc me and Priya on the outbound. Also ask finance for a 3-month reserved quote with a POC line-item discount. Oliver, mark this POC as billing: metered for now.
Oliver (SRE): Marked billing=metred. I'll follow up with finance numbers when available.
Maria - Sales: Great work team :thumbsup: End of thread.
